I have not tried playing your game, but here's a bit of feedback just from your post.
I think the most important thing would be to get some translation/proofreading services. You mention a publisher, so if you actually have a publisher perhaps they'll help you with this.
Regardless, the English in the game's description and the screenshots would definitely make me not buy this game if I saw it on Steam.
You only show a couple of maps, but there appear to be some mapping errors on that large house. Particularly the center area, as it goes from two-height walls down to a one-height wall where the house is - is that actually intended to be shorter? Like people have to crouch to get into the doorway?
(there's also a lot of very lined-up flowers and trees, even in the forest areas on the side)
Good luck with your project.

posts.author: hiddenone
posts.body:
Heyas, I played your demo and have some thoughts. I second Turan's comment about needing a proofreading service, you seem to want to tell a deep story but the current level of English isn't up to that task. Take some time to find yourself an English editor and get your dialogue polished.
Spoiler:
Feedback
Starting with the intro, please please
please
ditch the AI images. It isn't bringing anything to your game, and is actually likely to dissuade people from playing your game because AI is so often seen in lazy cash grab-type games. Custom art, free resources made by artists, or even maps made with RPG Maker would be better than oddly sized AI images. But at the moment, the game set me up to think that corners were cut in quality so the game could get released quickly.
The fact that the English is rough doesn't help the game either. I already mentioned finding an editor, and I want to really emphasize that because English isn't your first language. English is a mess of a language (and I say that as a native speaker), so writing dialogue that feels natural can be hard. That's where someone else can help you get your ideas across. As a quick example, here's part of your intro:
Do you believe in Ghost?
Honestly I do not believe in Ghost
Although I could see them...
Something that people thought were Ghost
They were natural fragments that been living among us. They recorded every moments and memories from the Past that need to be delivered
They attached each other and getting stronger then manifested into anything...
Click to expand...
And here is how I would rewrite it to flow better:
Do you believe in ghosts?
Honestly, I don't believe in them. Even though I can see ghosts, or at least what people think are ghosts.
They're natural echoes of the past that float in the world all around us. Records of every moment and memory that never reached their destination.
And these lost memories merge together, getting stronger and stronger, until they form into something new...
Click to expand...
Of course this isn't perfect either, but hopefully you can see the difference in how the sentences work together. A great story can be ruined by awkward writing, so make sure to give it all the time and care that it deserves so that players all feel the impact that you're aiming for.
I won't comment too much on the story itself, besides one thing: mixing historical events with fantasy can work but it needs a careful touch. You bring up WW2 in your description and in the game, but then renamed countries like the Empire of Zipan so is this a fantasy world and not based on real-life events? Inspiration from historical events is great, but I think you should change WW2 in the game to have a more generic or in-world fitting name so that it's not as jarring when the country names don't match up to what the player expects.
Moving on to the gameplay, there wasn't too much going on outside of battles in the demo so that's what I'll focus on. And while I see what you're going for with the battles and summoning beings that are strong against certain enemy types, I do think it needs a lot more tweaking and polishing to really work. Right now enemies do a lot of damage and cause turn-missing states often, so killing them as fast as possible is the best way to play. That means only using the summoning skills and ignoring any other option is the best option, meaning that there isn't much thinking involved in battles. I never used Taunting because I would rather have Arios use his summoning skills, and I gave up on Scan after it didn't do anything on a few enemies. So instead of spamming Attack, I was just spamming summoning skills. Adjusting the skills and enemy stats to allow for more choices in battles could make it more enjoyable.
The battle tutorial itself needs work too. I get that you want to have some fun with it, but having an aside about Final Dream and which game in the series is best doesn't help your player learn how to fight. You state that it's a turn-based battle system, but if your player doesn't know what that is then the tutorial isn't helpful at all. And having a comment about how today's kids think turn-based games are a waste of time is a terrible choice, why are you mocking your possible players? If you don't like turn-based, then you should take more time to create a battle system that you do enjoy.
I played until the end of the demo, and noticed that there was a major jump in difficulty with the enemies. I ended up getting a few game overs because enemies kept confusing my characters so I would just be sitting there for a few turns unable to do anything, and by the time I had control again my party was bleeding and ended up dying because their HP was just too low after healing compared to the damage enemies did. You should double-check how often enemies can inflict states and adjust it so that players have a chance during battles.
I noticed a few other bugs and oddities:
Game folder calls the game Soul Fragment in the zip, not Love of Mothers
Your chosen font has a kerning issue (the letters overlap, making it harder to read), may be good to look into it or choose a different font
There's a mix of tall sprites and MV-sized sprites which looks odd. Stick with one size for all adults
Scan doesn't work on every enemy, so it's not a useful skill at the moment
Overall, you clearly have a story you want to tell but right now the dialogue and gameplay is hampering that story. Take some time to find help with the writing, play around more with the combat, and I'm sure you'll see some incredible improvements.
Good luck with your project!

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
So, for disclosure, I have not played your demo.
But just to offer an opinion based on a few of the things that
@hiddenone
said and that I saw in the screenshots - it seems like your game is trying to be serious and satirical at the same time, and that just doesn't work well.
If the game is supposed to be comedy, then I'd suggest dropping the events of WW2 and serious-sounding ghost ideas.
If the game is supposed to be serious, leave out stuff like Empire of Zipan, jokes about other video games, and jokes about video game players.

Serious question: do you want battles to be an important part of your game or not? Games don't need to have battles to be engaging, so if you would prefer to focus on the story itself then taking more time to think on how the dream world functions would be good. Perhaps instead of battles the ghosts affect the dream landscape, meaning that the player has to solve puzzles to untangle the memories. Or you could go for a more visual novel-style game to fully focus on the emotional story.
But having battles that you want the players to rush through will just lead to a worse experience for players.
